title: The start of something new
summary:
A twisted fate awaited the party as they awoke amidst the rubble of what had once been the Silver Chalice. Shattered beams and broken stone told the story of sudden destruction, the work of a young dragon, its mind possessed by chaos.


Within moments, Waess noticed something was wrong. The dragon was sick. Without hesitation, he chose survival over confrontation, setting his sights on escape and rushing to bring himself to safety.


Ray, however, had other plans. Spotting a seemingly injured figure lying helplessly on the ground, he shot an arrow at the dragon, successfully drawing its attention away from the victim. 
The dragon’s gaze shifted and then it noticed Waess attempting to flee.


With a powerful beat of its wings, the dragon took off and struck Waess down, knocking him unconscious. Ray sprinted toward Waess’s fallen body, desperately trying to check on him. He placed himself between Waess's unconscious body and the dragon, standing as a shield.


The dragon struck Ray with the same brutal force, leaving him collpased on the ground beside Waess.


Amidst the chaos, Marvers focused on what he could still save. He moved through the wreckage, helping as many survivors as possible. His efforts failed at the last person, a woman with a broken leg, barely able to suppress her pain filled whimpers.


The dragon quickly noticed.


It lunged toward Marvers and sank its teeth into his shoulder, attempting to finish him off right where he stood.


“Just when it seems that all hope is lost, the three of you feel a sudden warmth, a resonance within the items that have guided your journey so far. Light bursts from each of your "special" items. Marvers’s holy symbol, Ray’s bolotie and Waess’s moon necklace. You begin to float off the ground, the light swirling around you, merging into a blinding magical explosion that shakes the Inn to its foundations.”


Everyone wakes up in the Monastery located on the very top of Guardians Height.


Waess and Ray talked things out regarding the attack right after they awoke, while Marvers checked on Martin and his newly found friend. Martin, worried, asked Marvers to find out whether his grandmother Lilia was safe.


Afterward, Waess struck up a conversation with Aarely. And through him, Marvers discovered that they shared the same religion.


Ray headed to the Main Hall to speak with Berta, a nun who lived in the monastery, about the deity Talona and this mysterious Person called Misha. During their conversation, he learned that Talona has an active temple in Duweil. Berta sent a messenger to a priest who was close to Misha to gather more information about her whereabouts.


Meanwhile, Marvers and Waess went to a small and diy'd temple (probably by Aarley) to pray to Soldea. Both of them individually prayed, received a subtle sign in response and then left. On their way back, Waess discovered a small note from Wilfen, written in Elvish using expensive purple ink. "Whoever can read this, Hello there :)"


Later, Ray went to the gardens by himself to inform Erwin (in his head) that everything was alright. While there, he too received a small sign making him feel assured that he is going to be alright, everything is going to be alright..

title: Leaving Guardians Height behind
summary:
The group found themselves still within the monastery. After Ray briefly left Waess and Marvers to explore the gardens, the two decided to further inspect the murals lining the monastery’s walls. Marvers noticed several explicit sexual depictions, including one portraying the three rulers of Lacrima, Duweil and Dredel engaged in intercourse, accompanied by an elvish inscription reading “Fuck Capitalism.” Marvers was deeply confused as to why such imagery was permitted on holy grounds.

Meanwhile, Waess cast Redraw and Rewrite, causing the letters of Wiltfen’s message to dance and transform into small, stick-like figures. He also commented that Marvers’ “Spine tale”, an element of Ivian culture seemed unusually short for his age. Marvers bluntly shut the conversation down, making it clear he did not wish to discuss it.

When Ray returned, he and Waess set off together with two goals: to find Aarely and to get Ray to a post office. On their way toward the monastery’s main entrance, the two shared a surprisingly intimate conversation, ending in Waess offering himself should Ray ever wish to explore intimacy with another man. The moment was abruptly interrupted by a passing monk. They asked him for directions to Aarely and the post office, then parted ways.

While this was happening, Marvers returned to the room left to where they had first awakened. After knocking, he heard a hushed “enter”and slowly opened the door to complete darkness. As he stepped inside, the door slammed shut behind him and a hand gripped his shoulder, startling him. Once his eyes adjusted, he saw a tall high elf, nearly his height, standing close behind him.

The elf seized Marvers arm and pulled him toward the altar, where he cast light on a wooden handle and pointed to a book. He wrote a single question: "What are you looking for?” Upon closer inspection, Marvers noticed how unsettling the elf appeared, long, straight black hair perfectly arranged down his back, a slim face, and a prominent scar running across his left eye. One eye was milky white, the other a piercing grey.

After a brief interaction, the elf guided Marvers out of the room, still holding his hand. As they left, Marvers caught a glimpse of someone lying in the darkness, a person with a fatal looking wound that did not bleed. Instead, the injury appeared grown over with grey, ashen wood. The figure made no sound, yet Marvers was convinced they were still alive. Shaken, he paused to steady himself before continuing his search for Layla.

Elsewhere, Waess found Aarely and pulled him out of an impending burnout by guilting him into joining Waess for a meal. They sat down at a small restaurant consisting of a bar counter and three tables, where they ate Meadowroot and Griftlon stew, a dish similar to one from Lacrima, though made with Griftlon meat (a large mountain bird) instead of rabbit. During the meal, Aarely revealed that his deity had sent him a sign: the group needed to leave the monastery as soon as possible.

Ray, meanwhile, made his way to the post office. There, he befriended the postal worker Matteo and struck a deal, informing Sir Halden about the mysterious letters he had been receiving and agreeing to write Matteo about the outcome.

After searching the entire monastery without success, Marvers entered the main hall, where he spoke with Berta. From her, he learned that Layla may have already been healed and released. He also uncovered grim historical knowledge: roughly 150 years ago, Queen Cyria Powsky ordered the eradication of all remaining dragons, resulting in a widespread witch hunt situation in which any being suspected of being a dragon was executed. 
When the group finally reunited, Aarely informed Marvers that Layla was in the Darkroom and infected. He instructed Ray to leave with the group, promising to deliver the priests reply as soon as possible.

On their way to the gate, Marvers put on his armor, revealing the King’s family crest once worn by Lacrima’s soldiers. The group quickly concealed it with Marvers scarf before proceeding. At the gate, they encountered Virex Halden, who offered to let them leave the village in exchange for interrogating them. As part of the deal, they were also to report what they had witnessed to a nearby Lacriman outpost.

Each member of the party was asked the same question. Afterward, Virex released them, just as Aarely arrived. He warned them quietly:

“Be careful. I hope to see you again soon. She who watches me from afar has shown me that no good comes from sharing the whole truth with those who serve Lacrima. Not telling is not lying. Be careful out there.”

And with that, the party made their way onward.

title: A warm welcome by Commander Halden
summary:
The party made their way down from Guardians’ Height after the first interrogation with Commander Virex Halden. The hike took about four hours, and by approximately 3PM, they began making their way through the forest.

Waesstan confronted Marvers about his suspicious behavior and expressed his concerns regarding Marvers possession of ancient Lacrimian military armor. In response, Marvers removed the chest plate displaying the crest and packed it away. Waesstan appreciated the gesture and the three of them continued onward.

As the two men walked ahead of Ray, discussing the matter, Ray began to feel as though he was being watched, triggering a familiar anxiety. He did not hesitate to voice his unease and Marvers quickly understood exactly what he meant, they were being observed. By whom or what remained unknown, but Marvers recalled Commander Halden saying something that could point to the possibility that someone might be following the group.

As they continued, the party searched for a safe place to spend the night. They found a clearing near the main path, hidden enough not to attract attention from anyone passing by. Waesstan settled down and bantered with Ray while Marvers gathered materials for a campfire. Once the fire was prepared, Marvers suggested going hunting to distract himself. Ray initially wanted to join, but after Waesstan insisted they stay together, he remained behind. Marvers promised to return in about an hour, saying, “If I am not back in an hour, you can assume I am late.” With that, he ventured into the forest.

Although he struggled at first, Marvers eventually managed to shoot an elk. The success brought back fond memories, which he briefly dwelled upon before slinging the elk over his shoulder and returning to camp.

Ray and Marvers skinned the deer together, with Ray showing Marvers the proper technique. Afterwards, they returned to camp and arranged the night watch schedule. Before everyone went to sleep, Ray recognized a song from his past that was just sung by Waesstan. Waesstan told Ray that it is an Ivian song and that he knows some of the dances from there. This lead to Ray dancing with Waesstan.

The feeling of being watched did not subside, and during the night, Marvers noticed two heads peeking out from a bush. At first, he assumed them to be small creatures like goblins, but they turned out to be two half elves, each a different type of spellcaster. The truth became apparent when one of them, panicked at being seen and attacked Marvers.

A brutal combat ensued. Marvers struck down the older brother, enraging the younger sibling, who relentlessly attacked Marvers and knocked him down three times before finally being struck by Waesstan’s magical attack, finishing him off. 

After the battle, Marvers inspected the bodies and Waesstan noticed a crest on both elves armor. They bore the family crest of the noble Montmorency family, a pink crescent moon cradling a silver rose. “Grace endures where steel fails.” Thats what the family stood for. The Montmorencys were a secretive, strategic noble house in Lacrima, playing key roles in both the War of Scaled Nature and smaller conflicts with other countries. Outwardly loyal to the royal family, they nonetheless pursued their own influence behind the scenes.

The current heads of the house were Lord Thalanil Montmorency and Lady Sariel Montmorency, who had seven children: Endyl, Lirael, Caelwyn, Sylvaen, Caelyth, Orin, and Syvil. The two halfelves the party had struck down were Endyl and Orin, with Orin being the older brother. Upon inspecting the bodies, Marvers found gold, several weapons, and a letter on them. 
"I shall be brief. Our informant has conveyed to us that the one now known as "Waesstan" makes his way towards Guardians Height. Should you encounter a circumstance that proves beyond your ability to manage, do not hesitate to withdraw. Fall back and summon assistance. No undertaking is worth risking your life.

Know that your mother’s concern mirrors my own. I place you in the care of Sune, hope you return unscathed from this operation.

Stay safe,
Thalanil Montomorency"

Marvers showed the letter to Waesstan and questioned him about the “Waesstan.” Waesstan confessed that he had previously gone by another name but, due to circumstances, had changed it.

The group stayed up for the rest of the morning and set out on their journey early. Along the way, they came across a small shrine dedicated to a fallen deity, one that Marvers had memories of from his past. This deity had been worshipped by one of his earlier companions. Seeing the shrine brought back memories of the last time he had seen her, when she had given Marvers her holy symbol after the deity had fallen. It was customary for followers of this deity to entrust the symbol to the most important person in their life to burn it as a signal that the era of belief had ended. She had asked Marvers to give it to the most important person in both of their lives: whether he had done so remained known only to him.

After snapping out of the memory, Marvers took a quiet moment for himself and placed one of his rings on the shrine before the group continued on.

A few hours later, the group arrived at the Stoneward Hideout, the outpost Commander Halden had sent them to. There, they were asked if they had a group name. Ray suggested “The Three Musky-tiers,” which was promptly shot down. The guards at the front gate allowed them entry and directed them to where they could find Commander Halden.

Inside the main building, the party found Commander Halden through a receptionist, who instructed them to go to Room 13. There, they saw Halden seated in a spacious room with an open fireplace and two red velvet sofas facing each other across a tea table. He was drinking tea and invited them to sit. He offered the party to stay for the night and continue the interrogation the next day. The party accepted the kind offer and dispersed, each taking some time for themselves before retiring for the evening.

Waesstan remained with Commander Halden a little longer, as he had received a letter from him. They discussed some matters, during which Halden casually referred to his family as the “King’s Dogs” adding that he did not see himself playing that role. The exact meaning of his remark remained unclear.

With that, the party safely settled at the outpost.
highlights: Being followed by Montmorency family members

title: Calm before the Storm at Stoneward Hideout
summary:
The party arrived at the Outpost and after speaking with Commander Virex Halden, settled in for the night. Following a longer private conversation with the Commander, Waesstan returned to the assigned room to meet Marvers and Ray. There, Marvers openly shared his plan to visit the bathhouse. The idea of a warm bath appealed to Waesstan and he decided to join Marvers.

Meanwhile, Ray chose to speak with Commander Halden about a sensitive matter. In exchange for Ray’s promise not to share the information with anyone, not even his companions, Halden revealed further details regarding the letters. Ray was also granted permission to use the Commander’s private bathhouse, where he bathed alone.

While Ray enjoyed his solitude, Waesstan and Marvers relaxed in the mixed bathhouse. There, they encountered a noblewoman named Selene Witword. She spoke with Marvers about Duweil and praised the beauty of the kingdom. Selene recommended visiting the Festival of Deep Lights and warned that the main road to Duweil was closed, advising instead that they take an alternate coastal route. When Waesstan pressed her for more details about her noble status, she politely ended the conversation and bid them farewell.

Afterward, Waesstan left before Marvers and went to the library to read. Ray soon joined him, though he appeared distant after learning a piece of information. Not long after, Waesstan departed the library and headed toward Commander Halden’s quarters.

Marvers arrived at the library shortly after Waesstan left. He commented on how pleasant Ray smelled, which offended Ray, likely due to mounting stress. They talked it out and continued reading, but at one point Ray noticed Marvers becoming increasingly distracted. Without a word, Marvers suddenly left the library and headed outside.

There, he spent time instructing a young soldier named Samuel on improving his swordsmanship before stopping at the canteen, where he ate and drank himself into a fogged, sluggish state. Ray eventually returned to the room, calming himself by gazing at the stars through the window until he was interrupted by a very drunk Marvers. Ray helped him into bed, then retired for the night himself.

Waesstan went to sleep much later, succumbing more to exhaustion than to any sense of restfulness.

The next morning, the group gathered for an interrogation. There, they learned the truth about Selene Witword and were questioned about their encounter with the Dragon on Guardian's Height. Afterward, they were promised a map to Duweil and sent on their way to the reception.

And thats where the Session ended.

title: New Truths and saying goodbye to Lacrima, for now
summary:
After the interrogation, the party made their way to the reception, where they received a map of Duweil from Marigold.

Marigold explained that she couldn’t draw the route herself, as she had never been to Duweil. Because of this, Waesstan and Ray went to see Selene Witword to have the directions marked onto the map, while Marvers decided to stay behind with Marigold.

When Waesstan and Ray arrived at the interrogation room, they found Selene sitting alone, surrounded by a pile of reports she still needed to complete. She greeted them warmly and gladly drew the route they would need to take. Selene recommended stopping at Thistlebrook along the way, suggesting they either purchase or borrow horses to make travel easier. Before leaving, Waesstan asked where he could find Commander Virex. Selene explained that Virex had left for duty and would not be at the outpost for the next few days. However, once the party reached Thistlebrook, Waesstan could send a priority letter that would reach Virex directly and immediately upon being sent. Selene also advised Ray and Waesstan to seek out the Magician to have their identification papers completed. Waesstan thanked her for the information, and he and Ray returned to the reception.

Meanwhile, Marvers was speaking with Marigold after retrieving the party’s bags from their room. Their conversation started off a bit awkward but quickly became friendlier. Marvers revealed that he had once worked as a soldier in Lacrima, which sparked Marigold’s curiosity. She asked where he had been stationed, and Marvers told her he had served at the Royal Palace in Wiffprint. The discussion shifted to vacations and holidays, during which Marigold admitted that she had never taken a vacation herself, as she usually sent her money home to support her family in Wiffprint. Moved by this, Marvers gave her five gold and encouraged her to take some time off. In return, Marigold promised to send him a letter to PencePost, a large post office in Fooch.

When the others returned, they asked about the Magician, and Marigold pointed them toward the canteen. There, they found a small elf, about 1.47 meters tall, wearing a black robe with purple stitching. Every Lacrimian wizard wore such a robe, with the stitching color indicating status, though none of the party knew what purple represented. The wizard, Serode, led them to the library and began the identification process.

The procedure involved asking a series of questions:

Name

Age

Species

Citizenship

Birthdate
To verify the answers, Serode cast a truth spell. This caused a slight complication for Marvers and Ray, as both claimed to be human, which was not entirely true. In the end, everyone received their papers, though Marvers’s species was officially listed as “Dragonborn.” Both Marvers and Ray were more than confused about the reveal of their identity.

Once the paperwork was completed, Ray stormed out of the room, brushing past Waesstan and Marvers as he hurried to the reception to collect his bag. He then went to the interrogation room to ask Selene about rations and she directed him back to the canteen. There, Ray met a cook named Michael and asked him about coffee. Michael explained that coffee was a luxury item and difficult to acquire. Waesstan and Marvers soon joined Ray and Michael joked about traveling with Marvers before wishing the group a safe journey.

And so, their travels began.

After only an hour or two, the group reached the border, where panic set in as they remembered the chestplate from Marvers’s armor still in their possession. To make matters worse, Marvers admitted the issue with his identity papers. Despite this, they chose to proceed with a risky plan. Ray distracted the border soldier while Waesstan acted overly affectionate toward Marvers, clinging to him to get close enough to the chestplate and cast Redraw Rewrite on the crest. The maneuver succeeded and the group continued onward.

As night fell, the party settled beneath a large tree in a field of tall grass. Marvers went off alone to bury the chestplate, digging with his bare hands and injuring them in the process. When he returned, Ray helped bandage his wounds and prepared a stew using their rations. After eating, they set up a watch rotation and went to sleep. Ray fell asleep on his watch, luckily Marvers woke up on his own.

During Marvers’s watch, he awoke to find four glowing eyes staring at him from the tree. This led to a fight against two bird like monstrosities. The party emerged victorious, but Marvers was infected with a condition known as Redding Ague. Ray rushed to him and cast Cure Wounds, healing his external injuries. Waesstan took over the final watch and the rest of the night passed peacefully.

And that’s how Session 5 ended.
